# /storyboard

## Purpose

Turn a shot list into boards: one or more frames per shot with precise
composition notes (framing, subject placement, eyeline, movement arrows),
optionally rendered as images. Boards are the cheapest place to catch a bad
composition or an uncuttable pair — a re-drawn frame costs cents; a
re-generated clip does not.

## Use When

- A scene has shots (from `/shot-list` or `/smart-shot`) and you want to see
  the cut before spending on keyframes.
- Composition or flow feels wrong in review — iterate at board level, then
  push fixes back into the shot files.
- Pitching the sequence to collaborators who need pictures, not YAML.

## Inputs

- `scene` (ID or path, required): the `SC_###` to board.
- `frames_per_shot` (string, optional, default `auto`): `auto` (extra frames
  for developing/moving shots) | integer.
- `render` (string, optional, default `sketch`): `text` (descriptions only,
  free) | `sketch` (image provider, line/tone style) | `styled` (image
  provider, in project LOOK).

## Invokes Agents

- storyboard-artist
- visual-director

## Required Skills

- storyboard-generation
- cinematography

## Process

1. Read every shot in order with its blocking and continuity fields; verify
   axis and screen-direction data exist (boards drawn without an axis are
   fiction).
2. storyboard-artist describes each frame: subject placement by thirds,
   headroom and lead room consistent with screen direction, foreground/
   midground/background layers, and arrows for subject and camera movement.
   Developing shots get start/key/end frames.
3. visual-director reviews the flip-through as a cut: compositions must
   contrast across cuts, eyelines must oppose across the axis, and the
   sequence's size rhythm must build where the scene builds.
4. If `render` is not `text` — **cost gate:** estimate frame count × provider
   rate, confirm before generating. Sketch style renders composition only;
   it deliberately avoids identity detail to stay cheap.
5. Assemble `storyboard.md` (frames in cut order with notes) and the board
   manifest mapping frames to shots and image files.
6. Any composition change that contradicts a shot file is pushed back into
   that `SH_*.yaml` — boards never silently fork from shots.

## Outputs

- `production/scenes/SC_###/storyboard/storyboard.md` — boards in cut order
  (human document, no schema).
- `production/scenes/SC_###/storyboard/board-manifest.yaml` — frame-to-shot
  map with image paths and render provenance (manifest, no schema).
- `production/generations/<batch>/generation-record.yaml` — one per rendered
  frame batch, validates against `schemas/generation-record.schema.json`.
- `production/scenes/SC_###/storyboard/board.html` — the composed one-page
  visual production board (characters, plates, data-faithful blocking floor
  plan, storyboard grid), built from approved assets via `npm run board --
  --scene-dir <dir>` (`scripts/build-board.js`). Nothing on it is generated;
  it is faithful composition and re-runs at any time.

## Notes

- `text` mode is free and often enough; render images when composition is
  genuinely in doubt or the sequence must be pitched.
- Boards are previs, not reference: never feed board frames into
  `/generate-keyframes` as identity references — that is what approved
  masters are for.
- Related: `/shot-list` / `/smart-shot` (upstream), `/generate-keyframes`
  (next paid step), `/continuity-review` (reads boards to spot-check flow).
